title: Etale algebras over a henselian local ring have unique sections through rational points of the closed fibre
statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] (henselian in the sense of idempotent lifting for finite $S$-algebras), let $S\to B$ be a ring map such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $\mathfrak q'\subset B$ be a prime ideal lying over $\mathfrak m$ such that the induced map of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] $\kappa=S/\mathfrak m\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is an isomorphism. Then there is exactly one homomorphism of $S$-algebras $\sigma:B\to S$ (a retraction of $S\to B$) with $\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak q'$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(8): proof reduces by Proposition Tag 00UE (proposition-etale-locally-standard) to a standard etale $S[t]_g/(f)$ ('details omitted'), lifts the simple root $a_0$ of $\bar f$ by the root-lifting definition of henselian (Definition Tag 04GF, definition-henselian), and gets uniqueness from Lemma lemma-uniqueness (just before 04GG). Stacks' definition of henselian is root lifting (04GF); [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] is idempotent lifting, so the split of this node also needs the equivalence (04GG (1)$\Leftrightarrow$(10), or More on Algebra Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex), (3)$\Leftrightarrow$(2): idempotent lifting for finite algebras is equivalent to lifting $A$-algebra maps $A'\to A/I$ from etale $A'$ to $A'\to A$, which gives existence directly)
